blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Real-time streaming video generation has gained rapid momentum in live content creation and interactive media. Deploying such systems in practice requires flexible scaling factors to accommodate diverse source resolutions, target displays, and computational budgets. However, extending fixed-scale generative video super-resolution (VSR) to varying target scales poses two challenges: downsampling from a larger fixed scale incurs redundant cost, while re-optimizing the diffusion transformer (DiT) is costly and alters the shared generative prior. To address both, we propose FlexVSR, a decoupled framework for continuous-scale streaming generative VSR with supervision at only a few scales. Our key insight is that naively resampling fixed-scale latents onto a new target grid induces scale-dependent input mismatch, which can be effectively addressed through parameter-efficient, scale-aware adaptation of the latent interface without updating the DiT. To this end, FlexVSR introduces ReLSA (Refined Latent Scale Adaptation), a lightweight latent adapter that constructs and refines target-grid latents before they enter the DiT, enabling a shared frozen VSR prior to generalize across continuous scales with only 0.274M trainable parameters and an adaptation cost of 7.3 H100 GPU-hours, while introducing no additional temporal dependencies and preserving the native causal streaming protocol. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive or superior reconstruction and temporal quality, lower latency than most native-scale streaming baselines and offline methods, and effective generalization to unseen continuous scales, filling the continuous-scale gap in real-time streaming generative VSR.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
High-resolution video generation does not require performing every operation at the target resolution. Modern video generation pipelines widely adopt a coarse-to-fine paradigm: synthesizing global semantics and temporal dynamics at low resolution (LR), followed by latent upsampling and high-resolution (HR) generative refinement [ 2 , 16 , 48 , 47 , 29 , 27 ] .
Within this paradigm, FlashVSR and InfVSR advance efficient streaming video
super-resolution (VSR) [ 49 , 46 ] .
Yet in practical real-time deployment, scaling must flexibly bridge varying source inputs, target resolutions, and tight compute budgets.
Moderate, non-integer scales offer finer control over this quality–compute trade-off, which requires operating directly on the requested grid rather than restoring at a higher
resolution and downsampling afterward, since both DiT computation and costly pixel decoding [ 21 ] scale steeply with output resolution. However, directly applying a fixed-scale model to naively resampled target-grid latents substantially degrades reconstruction quality, motivating lightweight scale adaptation of existing generative super-resolution (SR)
priors.

For flexible scaling, image restorers have explored scale-conditioned
upsampling in Meta-SR [ 20 ] and continuous coordinate
querying in LIIF [ 9 ] .
In the video domain, discriminative methods such as BasicAVSR [ 36 ] support online arbitrary-scale restoration yet lack generative priors for realistic detail synthesis.
Meanwhile, generative approaches such as VEnhancer [ 16 ] and AVSR-Diff [ 43 ] combine diffusion priors with flexible spatiotemporal enhancement or continuous decoding, but rely on multi-step sampling and temporal lookahead that constrain real-time streaming deployment.
Rather than designing and training an arbitrary-scale streaming diffusion model from scratch, we ask a more practical question: can an existing fixed-scale streaming generative VSR system be extended to continuous scales while strictly preserving its one-step causal inference protocol?

blocks.en: 2.1 Continuous-Scale SR and Latent Upsampling
blocks.zh: 2.1 连续抽样抽样

blocks.en:
Continuous-scale SR aims to reconstruct arbitrary target grids with a single
model. In single-image SR, Meta-SR [ 20 ] predicts scale-conditioned
filters, ArbSR [ 39 ] adapts scale-specific networks via
plug-in modules, and implicit approaches such as LIIF [ 9 ] ,
LTE [ 23 ] , and CiaoSR [ 4 ] query continuous
coordinates using local features, Fourier textures, or attention ensembles.
Extending to video, VideoINR [ 10 ] models continuous
space–time representations, SAVSR [ 24 ] combines
scale-adaptive convolution with spatiotemporal upsampling, and
LDIP [ 1 ] couples long-distance propagation with a
reusable arbitrary-scale feature upsampler.
While these methods achieve continuous-scale spatial upsampling, their viability for streaming deployment depends on temporal aggregation design.
For instance, ST-AVSR [ 35 ] attends to both past and
future frames, requiring future-frame lookahead, whereas
BasicAVSR [ 36 ] explicitly provides online, limited-lookahead, and offline variants. While effective for pixel-space reconstruction, such discriminative designs focus on distortion-oriented regression rather than generative synthesis, whereas reusing a frozen latent restorer requires prior-compatible target-grid latents.
Meanwhile, generative approaches leverage diffusion priors through multi-step, offline temporal processing. VEnhancer [ 16 ] jointly enhances spatial and temporal resolution, using ≥ \geq 15 sampling steps and overlapping chunks for long videos [ 15 ] . AVSR-Diff [ 43 ] denoises on an LR latent grid to limit computational growth with output scale, combining with 50 sampling steps and a bidirectional continuous decoder. LUVE [ 47 ] instead places latent upsampling at discrete scales between low-resolution generation and offline high-resolution content refinement. Thus, causal, continuous-scale generative VSR remains an open challenge.

blocks.zh: 2.2 流媒体视频超分辨率

blocks.en:
Unlike offline restorers relying on bidirectional
propagation [ 6 , 7 ] or multi-step
diffusion [ 48 ] , streaming generative VSR must jointly
constrain temporal lookahead and denoising steps.
Through one-step distillation, FlashVSR [ 49 ] combines
locality-constrained sparse attention with lightweight conditional decoding,
while InfVSR [ 46 ] pairs a causal DiT with rolling KV
caching.
For latent generation cascades, SoL-Refiner [ 27 ] achieves
fast one-step high-resolution refinement, while Ultra
Flash [ 29 ] further enables real-time streaming via causal
latent upsampling and cascaded one-step refinement.
Since these models are tailored to fixed target scaling factors, extending them to arbitrary target grids requires either extra native-scale computation and decoding before downsampling or direct frame or latent resizing with reduced reconstruction quality.

blocks.en:
Diffusion models [ 18 , 34 ] , diffusion

powerful, reusable generative priors.
To adapt frozen backbones, parameter-efficient tuning such as
LoRA [ 19 ] and side-branch controllers including
ControlNet [ 44 ] and T2I-Adapter [ 31 ] train
lightweight modules without updating base weights.
In super-resolution, StableSR [ 38 ] uses a time-aware
encoder for image SR, while LiteVSR [ 5 ] conditions a frozen
video DiT on low-quality inputs and intermediate denoising states.
Unlike fixed-scale adapters that inject internal conditioning into offline DiTs, FlexVSR unifies continuous upsampling and streaming restoration by adapting only the upstream latent interface, generalizing a frozen one-step causal DiT across target grids from sparse scale supervision while preserving its weights and causal protocol.

blocks.en: To enable continuous-scale streaming VSR without degrading restoration quality through direct latent resampling, FlexVSR operates in two decoupled stages (Fig. 2 ): one-time preparation of a reference-scale streaming SR prior, followed by lightweight upstream latent adaptation via ReLSA across continuous scales.

Compared systems. Focusing on adapting generative VSR priors, we primarily compare FlexVSR with representative fixed- and multi-scale generative VSR systems across streaming and offline settings.
Most compared systems use a Wan2.1-1.3B [ 41 ] DiT, including
FlashVSR [ 49 ] (with Tiny -T and
Full -F decoders), whereas LiteVSR [ 5 ] uses Wan2.2-5B [ 41 ] (official 5-step setting) and VEnhancer uses an I2VGen-XL 3D U-Net

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We present FlexVSR, unlocking practical continuous-scale capability for streaming generative VSR by adapting only the upstream latent interface of a frozen SR DiT.
Specifically, our 0.274 0.274 M-parameter ReLSA adapter is optimized end-to-end for frozen-prior compatibility in just 7.3 7.3 H100 GPU-hours while preserving the original causal streaming protocol.
Delivering favorable quality-latency trade-offs across unseen continuous scales, FlexVSR establishes a restoration paradigm that is flexible in both inference-time scaling and lightweight prior adaptation.
In practice, FlexVSR accommodates two complementary use cases: adapting varying low-resolution inputs to a fixed display resolution and mapping a fixed source stream to different target resolutions.
This allows flexible scale adjustments offline or across streams without scale-specific retraining, while pointing toward dynamic scale switching during live generation and playback. We hope our work inspires future research on achieving both low latency and high visual quality in streaming and interactive video generation.

我们介绍FlexVSR,解锁实际的连续规模能力,仅通过对冷冻的SR DiT的上游潜伏界面进行调适来进行流转基因VSR.
特别是我们的0.2740.274 M参数 ReLSA适配器在仅7.3个H100 GPU小时的冷冻前置兼容性上优化了端到端,同时保留了原因果流协议.
FlexVSR在不为人知的连续规模中作出有利于质量与相关性的权衡,建立了一种恢复模式,在推论时间尺度和轻量级之前的适应方面都具有灵活性。
在实践中,FlexVSR可以容纳两个互补的用途案例:将不同的低分辨率输入修改为固定显示分辨率,并将固定源流映射为不同的目标分辨率.
这使得灵活的规模调整能够脱线或跨流而无需针对规模的再培训,同时指向在现场生成和播放期间动态规模转换. 我们希望我们的工作激励未来在流媒体和互动视频生成方面实现低延迟和高视觉质量的研究。

Table S6 compares this model against FlashVSR-T D and Ultra Flash N , the two fastest low-latency streaming baseline configurations in main-paper Table 2. All results use the same 40 YouHQ40 videos, original HR targets, and full-frame post-SR RGB metrics. FlashVSR-T (Tiny) uses its TCDecoder and full-canvas inference without additional spatial DiT tiling. Despite keeping the 2 × 2\times -only SR DiT frozen, the wider-scale FlexVSR model achieves the best overall average rank (1.16) and leads all three metrics across all 14 test scales from 1.2 × 1.2\times through 3 × 3\times . Against the native- 4 × 4\times FlashVSR-T D , it improves PSNR by 0.17–3.60 dB at every tested factor through 3.5 × 3.5\times , while FlashVSR-T D regains lower LPIPS and tLPIPS from 3.25 × 3.25\times onward and higher PSNR at its native 4 × 4\times scale. Against Ultra Flash N , FlexVSR is better on all three metrics at every tested factor except tLPIPS at 4 × 4\times . Overall, serving continuous scales with a single lightweight adapter on a frozen prior provides a practical balance among restoration quality, target-grid efficiency, and deployment flexibility for streaming video generation.

blocks.en:
Under this identical protocol, the Wan2.1-14B variant improves PSNR by 0.04–0.31 dB and lowers LPIPS over Wan2.1-1.3B at all four evaluated scales.
It also lowers tLPIPS at 1.5 × 1.5\times , 1.8 × 1.8\times , and 2 × 2\times .
These results indicate that ReLSA can benefit from the larger Wan backbone at both supervised and unseen scales.
Across distinct model families, however, sharing the same Stage-1 preparation recipe does not guarantee equally strong reference-scale priors.
In particular, the MiniMax-H3 VAE uses 16 × 16\times spatial compression with 24 latent channels, compared with 8 × 8\times spatial compression and 16 channels for Wan2.1, so identical RGB training crops map to coarser latent grids.
Moreover, encoding and decoding the HR YouHQ40 frames with the VAE alone, without ReLSA or the SR DiT, reaches 30.68 dB PSNR for MiniMax-H3 versus 32.66 dB for Wan2.1.
Differences in Stage-1 prior effectiveness and this lower VAE reconstruction baseline may both contribute to MiniMax-H3’s lower end-to-end scores in Table S7 , although the present comparison does not isolate individual factors.
Across the tested scales, relative trends remain consistent: the unseen 1.2 × / 1.8 × 1.2\times/1.8\times scales stay within 1.25 dB of the supervised scales on MiniMax-H3, comparable to the Wan2.1 backbones (1.05/1.24 dB).

它还将tLPIPS降低到1.5×1.5\时,1.8×1.8\时,2×2\时.
这些结果表明,ReLSA可以在监督和无形的尺度上受益于更大的万恩骨干。
但是,在不同的模范家庭中,分享相同的第一阶段准备方法并不能保证同样强大的参考尺度前科。
特别是MiniMax-H3 VAE使用16×16\times空间压缩,拥有24个潜伏通道,而Wan2.1则使用8×8\times空间压缩和16个潜伏通道,因此RGB训练作物图完全相同,可以压缩潜伏网格.
